correctness.rationale: Direct inversion of 2x2 Gram gives R_B=q_B(Xbar)/S+b11/m, with S=sum_i(Xi-Xbar)^2, q_B(t)=(-t,1)B(-t,1)^T>0. Orthogonal decomp X=t*1+u in mean direction and H={sum u=0} has Lebesgue Jacobian sqrt(m). The event R_B>z is exactly a shrinking (m-1)-ball of squared radius q_B(t)/(z-b11/m). Rescale u by sqrt(z-b11/m), apply pointwise continuity of p and dominated convergence (bounded compact p, fixed B) for a finite positive coefficient; endpoint t is null set. Layer cake gives moment iff s<(m-1)/2. Holder with q_B^rho and int p=1 yields integral >= (int q_B^-1/2)^(1-m); equality requires unique positive continuous p*_B. Independent exact-rational inverse Gram checks, small-scatter volume and m=2 integral tail computations independently corroborate finite cases. Infinite asymptotics rest on dominated convergence and Holder.
residual_risks: The optimality objective is the leading z→infinity tail constant, not any finite-threshold failure probability, classical A-optimal design or adaptive design.
Positive definiteness of B, iid continuous compactly supported p, fixed m>=2 are essential.

originality.rationale: Randomized least-squares conditioning and inverse-covariance lower tails are established, as are finite-pool joint volume-sampling experimental designs. The candidate identifies an exact collision-tube coefficient for iid continuous affine designs and its uniquely optimal density across all m. Those statements were not found in inspected modern primary theorems, and different sampling models/criteria prevent immediate implication.
residual_risks: A pre-existing small-ball/tube asymptotic for affine random design could imply the coefficient and an optimal design via a routine Hölder calculation; priority beyond inspected papers is provisional.
Additional treatment of design distributions with continuous inputs may give an equivalent optimizer under other statistical names.
